stages.headline: Arrangements of k out of n are ordered selections of k elements; there are Aₙᵏ = n(n − 1)…(n − k + 1) of them.
stages.headlineEnglish: Arrangements of k out of n are ordered selections of k elements; there are Aₙᵏ = n(n − 1)…(n − k + 1) of them.

stages.headline: The product rule: if the first choice can be made in m ways and the second in n ways, the pair can be chosen in m · n ways.
stages.headlineEnglish: The product rule: if the first choice can be made in m ways and the second in n ways, the pair can be chosen in m · n ways.

stages.headline: Aₙᵏ = n!/(n − k)!, where n! = 1 · 2 · … · n; three medallists from 10 can be chosen in A₁₀³ = 720 ways.
stages.headlineEnglish: Aₙᵏ = n!/(n − k)!, where n! = 1 · 2 · … · n; three medallists from 10 can be chosen in A₁₀³ = 720 ways.
